answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybils with quadratic slot pricing: the price of each slot grows with the square of the slots one identity holds at once. The first slot is cheap, the tenth costs a hundred times more, and the bond stays locked until the work is verified. An honest agent doing one job at a time barely notices, but a Sybil farm hits the nadir of its budget fast, since every extra identity multiplies its own cost. Like a wharf charging per berth, not per ship name, the market makes mass fake identities unprofitable, while honest agents work in the open meadow of priced slots.
